gaps: PROVENANCE CONTRADICTION (M7): the plan rules frontier-API-generated training data DEAD as 'radioactive for DARPA provenance,' yet M7's entire sovereignty corpus is TinyStories, which is GPT-3.5/GPT-4-generated synthetic data (VERIFIED: https://huggingface.co/datasets/roneneldan/TinyStories, license cdla-sharing-1.0). The 'own data' clause in M7's DARPA framing is impeachable as written. Fix: either argue the distinction explicitly in the provenance ledger (third-party-published dataset under CDLA-Sharing-1.0, not program-generated API output) and soften 'own data' to 'openly licensed data,' or pick a non-LLM-generated tiny corpus.

SAME CONTRADICTION IN M2, TWICE: (a) Tulu-3 contains WildChat GPT-4, 100K OpenAI-model-generated samples (VERIFIED: https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/tulu-3-sft-mixture) — dropping only the CC-BY-NC No Robots subset does not satisfy the plan's own doctrine; the ledger needs a per-subset generator-model column, not just a license column. (b) SmolTalk's largest subset Magpie-Ultra (400K samples) was generated with Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct (VERIFIED: https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceTB/smoltalk); the Llama 3.1 Community License requires models trained on Llama outputs to carry 'Llama' at the start of the model name plus license flow-down — this hits M6's naming/branding in the DARPA package and is nowhere in the License flow-down USER ACTION (which covers only TII and Meta-Llama-3-for-M8).

DEPENDENCY ORDER ERROR (M2->M5->M6): M2 re-tokenizes the mix to the Falcon-E 32,768 vocab BEFORE M5 selects the M6 vehicle. If M5b (bitnet-sft on BitNet-2B-4T, Llama-3 128,256-token tokenizer) wins — and the plan says prefer it since it targets the canonical model — the mix must be fully re-tokenized and re-sized. Fix: keep the M2 mix in text form with counts recorded for BOTH tokenizers, finalize sizing after the M5 decision.

M0 'TONIGHT' COLLIDES WITH THE LIVE EVAL: aegis-eval is running NOW (PID 888, ~972MB RSS, 93% CPU, ~24h to go; only ~1.6GB RAM available, MEASURED via ps/free). Loading transformers BitNet-2B for the M0 reference pass (multi-GB RSS) will swap-thrash, can OOM-kill either job, and invalidates the running eval's timing numbers per the plan's own memory-pressure-cliff finding. M0 slips ~24h, which slips M1; the schedule should say so explicitly.

M7 GATE IS UNMEASURABLE AS WRITTEN: 'on-corpus PPL tracks the half-size-fp16 expectation' references a half-size fp16 twin PPL that no experiment produces. Either schedule the twin (a ~5-7M fp16 model at the measured 733+ tok/s is ~1-3 days — cheap, and it doubles as the honest-comparison baseline DARPA will ask for) or replace the gate with published TinyStories-class baselines cited in advance. As written this is also a measurement-integrity violation: a reported comparison with no runtime computation behind one side.

M6 GATE REFERENCES A DOMAIN EVAL THAT NOTHING BUILDS: 'domain evals improve on the engine artifact' — no experiment defines or constructs a held-out domain eval set (M3's tiny suite is general-capability only; M2 builds training data only). Define the held-out domain eval (items, metric, engine-side harness format) inside M2 or M3, before M6 starts. Same issue in miniature for M4b: 'beats the hard prompt' needs a pre-registered held-out metric or it degenerates to eyeballing.

WEEK 1-2 CHROMEBOOK OVERSUBSCRIPTION + M6/M7 COLLISION: M3 overnight baselines (13-22h transformers-side), M4a/M4b (3-5 days, 'box idle'), M5a (hours), and M1 eval all claim the single box in weeks 1-2 under a one-heavy-job rule — the calendar needs an explicit serial order. Bigger: M6's before/after full M3 battery (another ~13-22h transformers-side plus engine runs) lands in weeks 2-4, exactly M7's 5-12-day exclusive box ownership. State explicitly: M6 full battery completes before M7 starts, or waits until M7 ends.

DISK BUDGET HAS NO EVICTION PLAN: 30GB free (MEASURED, df). M1 masters ~7GB land locally before mirroring; M2 raw downloads <10GB plus re-tokenized copies (x2 if the dual-tokenizer fix is adopted); fresh lm-eval venv ~2-5GB; M7 checkpoints; M9b Bonsai 2-16GB parked. Sum plausibly exceeds 30GB mid-program. Add a rule: verify external-drive mirror, then delete local masters before M2 downloads begin; log df before every multi-day run.

M1 HARDWARE DEPENDENCY NOT IN USER ACTIONS: the M1 gate requires booting the packed 3B on a real 2GB pre-AVX2 fleet box within a 1-2 day window. Physical access/prep of that machine (USB, UEFI setup) is a user-only action and is missing from the USER ACTIONS list (same applies to M7's final gate).

MINOR MISSING MODALITY (flag, not blocker): activation steering / control vectors over the frozen ternary models — zero-training, computed locally from a few hundred forward passes, applied in-engine as a per-layer bias add (bounded kernel change), published prior art (representation engineering / repeng). It is the only unconsidered capability-injection lever in the same class as M4 soft prompts and would be a cheap hedge if M4a's logit-parity gate fails; UNVERIFIED whether it composes well with ternary quantization — that is precisely the experiment.
verdict: The plan is sound enough to execute — gates are ordered cheap-before-expensive and the kill criteria are mostly real — but it must first resolve the self-contradiction that its own DEAD verdict on LLM-generated training data applies to TinyStories (M7) and to Tulu-3/SmolTalk subsets (M2/M6, including a Llama-license naming flow-down), defer the M2 tokenization choice until M5 picks the vehicle, push M0 past the currently-running 24h eval, and give M7's half-size-fp16 gate and M6's domain-eval gate concrete measurable baselines.
